arxiv-2201-01681.title: Making Music Using Two Quantum Algorithms
arxiv-2201-01681.creator: Euan J. Allen, Jacob F. F. Bulmer, Simon D. Small
arxiv-2201-01681.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Euan J. Allen, Jacob F. F. Bulmer, Simon D. Small. This document explores how to make music using quantum computing algorithms. The text is an unedited pre-publication chapter which will appear in the book “Quantum Computer Music”, Miranda, E. This chapters provides the background and specific details of a collaboration formed in 2021 between the Quantum Engineering Technology Labs - a quantum computing and technology research group at the University of Bristol - and music artist, producer and audio engineer Simon Small.

arxiv-2403-06411.title: Effect of non-equilibrium thermochemistry on Pitot pressure measurements in shock tunnels (or: Is 0.92 really the magic number?)
arxiv-2403-06411.creator: Tamara Sopek , Peter Jacobs, Suria-Devi Subiah, Peter Collen, and Matthew McGilvray
arxiv-2403-06411.description: Abstract Pitot pressure is the most common measurement in high total enthalpy shock tunnels for test condition verification. Nozzle calculations using multi-temperature non-equilibrium thermochemistry are needed in conjunction with Pitot measurements to quantify freestream properties. Pitot pressure is typically matched by tuning the boundary layer transition location in these simulations.

arxiv-2505-20355.title: GraLoRA: Granular Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2505-20355.creator: Yeonjoon Jung, Daehyun Ahn, Hyungjun Kim, Taesu Kim, Eunhyeok Park
arxiv-2505-20355.description: Abstract Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is a popular method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of generative models, valued for its simplicity and effectiveness. Despite recent enhancements, LoRA still suffers from a fundamental limitation: overfitting when the bottleneck is widened. It performs best at ranks 32–64, yet its accuracy stagnates or declines at higher ranks, still falling short of full fine-tuning (FFT) performance.

arxiv-2506-16788.title: Non-collinear magnetism contra frustration: Magnetic order and anisotropy in hexagonal MnPtGa. Preprint: Fecher; MnPtGa August 10, 2026
arxiv-2506-16788.creator: Gerhard H. Fecher, Roshnee Sahoo, Claudia Felser
arxiv-2506-16788.description: Abstract MnPtGa is a hexagonal intermetallic compound with a rich variety of magnetic order. Its magnetic state is reported to range from collinear ferromagnetism, to non-collinear skyrmion type order. MnPtGa is a system with strongly localized magnetic moments at the Mn atoms as was demonstrated using calculations for disordered local moments.

arxiv-2602-21635.title: A diffusion approximation for systems with frequent weak resetting
arxiv-2602-21635.creator: Tobias Galla
arxiv-2602-21635.description: Abstract We develop a diffusion approximation for systems subject to fast random resetting by small amplitudes. Equivalently, this describes systems with frequent but small catastrophes. We demonstrate the validity of the approximation by computing the stationary distribution and mean first-passage times of simple one-dimensional systems.

pmc-12745968.title: An Evidence-Based Exercise Program for Total Hip Arthroplasty Rehabilitation in Geriatric Patients with Femoral Neck Fractures: A Delphi Study

pmc-13052076.title: SLC52A1 is a neofunctionalized primate urate transporter enabling intestinal urate secretion
pmc-13052076.creator: Syunsuke Yamamoto, Katsuhisa Inoue, Tomoya Yasujima, Hideki Takei, Takahiro Yamashiro, Keiko Asai, Isamu Matake, Sora Uchiyama, Kinya Ohta, Hisanao Kishimoto, Kei Higuchi, Hisashi Anayama, Yuuko Asao, Hideki Hirabayashi, Nobuyuki Amano, Toru Shimizu, Tappei Takada, Takashi Tamura, Kenji Wakai, Yusuk
pmc-13052076.description: Serum urate levels are high in hominoids because of the evolutionary loss of uricase, an enzyme involved in purine metabolism during evolution. However, the mechanism underlying uricase loss remains unclear. We report the involvement of the neofunctionalized solute carrier family 52 member A1 (SLC52A1) in the evolutionary loss of uricase.

pmc-13056995.title: Human values and physical activity before and during COVID-19 restrictions in Hungary
pmc-13056995.creator: Gergely Csurilla, Imre Fertő, Zsófia Benedek, József Fogarasi, Zoltán Bakucs
pmc-13056995.description: Physical inactivity is a major public health challenge in Hungary. Drawing on Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Human Values, we exploit a natural experiment created by temporary population-wide restrictions to examine how value orientations relate to physical activity across contrasting contexts.

pmc-13081739.title: Motor cortical areas facilitate schema-mediated integration of new motor information into memory
pmc-13081739.creator: Serena Reverberi, Nina Dolfen, Bradley Ross King, Geneviève Albouy
pmc-13081739.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). New information is rapidly learned when it is compatible with pre-existing knowledge, that is, with a previously acquired schematic representation of the learned information. The influence of pre-established schema on learning has been extensively studied in the declarative memory domain, where it was shown that schema-compatible information could be rapidly assimilated into neocortical storage, bypassing the slow hippocampo-neocortical memory transfer process. Schema-mediated learning was recently examined in the motor memory domain; however, its neural substrates remain unknown.

pmc-13183763.title: 6-Hydroxyflavone Attenuates Inflammatory Osteolysis by Inhibiting Osteoclast Activation via the Nrf2 and Calcium Signaling Pathways
pmc-13183763.creator: Kun Qian, Qizhen Lu, Weiyi Wang, Qige Lu, Shenghong Dai, Chuanyun Fu, Shui Sun
pmc-13183763.description: Inflammatory osteolysis (IO) is a pathological bone disorder characterized by excessive osteoclast activation and bone resorption driven by inflammatory mediators and oxidative stress. 6-Hydroxyflavone (6-HOF), a natural flavonoid with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, has not been fully investigated in the context of IO.

pmc-13188380.title: Clarifying comparative claims in digital cognitive assessment: a matters arising on multimodal detection of cognitive impairment and amyloid positivity
pmc-13188380.creator: Paul W. Estes
pmc-13188380.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Digital cognitive assessments represent an important and rapidly evolving approach to detecting cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease–related pathology. report promising findings using a multimodal digital clock and recall assessment to identify cognitive impairment and amyloid positivity. While this contribution is welcomed, several comparative statements regarding Cognivue® rely on historical regulatory data and do not reflect the contemporaneous peer-reviewed evidence base available at the time of manuscript preparation.

pmc-13242181.title: eMZed 3: flexible and interactive development of scalable LC-MS/MS data analysis workflows in python
pmc-13242181.creator: Uwe Schmitt, Jethro Hemmann, Nicola Zamboni, Julia A Vorholt, Patrick Kiefer, Guoqiang Yu
pmc-13242181.description: SummaryLiquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) data analysis requires adaptable software solutions to meet diverse analytical needs. We present eMZed 3, a modern Python framework for flexible and interactive analysis of LC-MS/MS data. eMZed 3 enables users to develop scalable workflows tailored to their specific requirements while leveraging Python’s extensive ecosystem of libraries.

pmc-13556516.title: 868. Relation between arousal, motivation and attention, and effects of stimulant ADHD medication
pmc-13556516.creator: J Andreasen
pmc-13556516.description: BackgroundThis talk will explore contemporary neurobiological hypotheses of ADHD with a focus on two converging frameworks: arousal dysregulation and deficient reward processing. Central to the arousal account is the Yerkes–Dodson relationship, which proposes an inverted-U association between arousal and attentional performance.
